text:
sara_support: FYI customer reported tool-calling outputs getting associated with the wrong tool when we fan out calls in parallel. They see tool_result ids swapped across two simultaneous tool calls.

lee_eng: Can you paste the original request + response logs and the correlation ids? Also what runtime/version and model variant?

sara_support: Summary from customer: high QPS burst, using Redwood hosted API, two tools invoked in parallel via function calling. Observed: tool A output attached to tool B in call records, billing shows tokens charged to tool A but content from B. Severity P1 for them. Repro steps below.

sara_support: Request sample (redacted keys):
```json
{"model":"gpt-infer-3","input":"process order","tools":[{"name":"order-lookup","schema":{"order_id":"string"}},{"name":"pricing","schema":{"order_id":"string"}}],"tools_call_mode":"parallel","client_correlation_id":"cust-req-42","request_id":"req-20280301-1"}
```

sara_support: Response fragment from customer logs (they included engine logs):
```text
2028-03-01T15:02:10Z trace=tr-86 req=req-20280301-1 tool_call: order-lookup -> tool_result.id=tr-86-r1 content="Price: $X"
2028-03-01T15:02:10Z trace=tr-86 req=req-20280301-1 tool_call: pricing -> tool_result.id=tr-86-r2 content="Order: #12345"
2028-03-01T15:02:10Z svc=api router: associating tool_result.id=tr-86-r1 -> tool_name=pricing
```
They see the two tool_result ids and the final association shows r1 attached to pricing (swapped).

mike_sre: That's concerning. Could be a correlation header mixup in the parallel fanout path or a race in the result aggregator. Any batching/continuous-batcher logs? Also which runtime build?

sara_support: They said runtime v1.8.2, serving pool: dedicated-east-1, batcher=continuous, avg seq_len=80, burst QPS ~120 req/s.

lee_eng: Repro is high-value. Two hypotheses: (1) the correlation token in internal fanout isn't unique per subcall when parallelized (we've seen header reuse bug), (2) a queue reorder in the result demux where ordering index used is non-atomic under heavy load. Need request traces. Can you ask for a full trace from trace=tr-86?

sara_support: Asked customer for full trace and their SDK call code. They provided a minimal repro using Node SDK calling Promise.all on client.callTool for both tools. Code snippet: 
```js
// repro.js
const a = client.callTool('order-lookup',{order_id:'12345'});
const b = client.callTool('pricing',{order_id:'12345'});
await Promise.all([a,b]);
```
They said switching to sequential (await a; await b) removed the issue.

mike_sre: That strongly points to a parallel correlation/ID allocation or demux concurrency bug. If sequential fixes it, temp mitigation for customer = force sequential or add unique per-tool correlation header.

anna_pm: Escalating to eng-runtime. Can someone triage and add to triage board? Tagging @lee_eng. Customer impact: P1 (incorrect tool outputs + billing misattribution).

lee_eng: I'll repro locally. Plan: run a harness with continuous batcher, 120 QPS, Promise.all style parallel calls, and instrument internal correlation header X-RW-Subcall-Id and the aggregator's demux. If we reproduce, will bisect runtime commits between 1.7.x and 1.8.2.

lee_eng: Quick mitigation patch ideas: make subcall id allocation strictly unique (use UUID v4) and attach per-subcall seq number. Also ensure aggregator matches on (request_id, subcall_id) not on a shared header.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: created issue INF-4921 in eng-runtime backlog with label=customer-P1, owner=lee_eng.

sara_support: Customer accepted workaround (sequential) for now but wants permanent fix. They want ETA for fix + whether we'll remediate billing mischarges retroactively.

mike_sre: For billing, we need to audit token attribution for req=req-20280301-1..req-20280301-20 (customer provided range). I'll start a token attribution audit job with trace join. Could be a one-off mismatch if aggregator wrote tool_name incorrectly.

lee_eng: Repro steps I'm running and logs to collect: 1) run harness with n=5000 parallel requests, Promise.all style 2) capture internal header X-RW-Subcall-Id, correlation_id, request_id 3) snapshot aggregator map state at high load 4) check if demux pops wrong id. If reproduced I'll attach minimal failing trace and put a hotfix branch.

sara_support: Adding customer's billing contact and legal cc. I'll coordinate comms once we have repro and remediation plan.

anna_pm: Please update INF-4921 with ETA and rollback plan. Keep support looped.

lee_eng: Will update within 4h after first repro attempt. If reproduced, hotfix target EOD.

sara_support: Thanks everyone. Customer waiting, will share workaround details (sequential calls) and escalate billing audit. :pray:

lee_eng: Logs I'm capturing (snippet):
```text
[aggregator] recv result subcall_id=uuid-7a1 req=req-20280301-1 -> enqueue
[aggregator] recv result subcall_id=uuid-7a2 req=req-20280301-1 -> enqueue
[aggregator] demux pop -> mapping[subcall_id] = ??? (race detected)
```
If anyone on runtime wants to pair, ping me.

mike_sre: Also adding a temporary server-side guard: if tool_call_mode==parallel and internal batcher >1 then attach enforced unique subcall ids and validate mapping on write; log any mismatch at WARN level to help audit.

sara_support: Noted. Will inform customer and share INF-4921 link.

lee_eng: thanks, starting repro now.

infra-bot: issue INF-4921 updated by lee_eng: initial repro attached.

sara_support: Closing loop here once we have hotfix + billing audit results.
